name: Seb Seliyer
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: 'a Gypsy variety not known to be immediately related to any other Gypsy language' (Firuzkuh, Iran); no descriptive source listed or located.

sources.citation: Windfuhr, Gernot L. 2002 [updated 2012]. "GYPSY ii. Gypsy Dialects". Encyclopaedia Iranica XI/4, pp. 415-421 (online edition).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The whole article contains no occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent'. Seb-Seliyer gets two sentences: 'The dialect of the Seb-Seliyer, literally "tin-workers," which is spoken in a cluster of mountain villages near Firuzkuh (Sotuda). While largely adapted to local Mazandarani, its small but distinct core vocabulary has remained a linguistic isolate, except for a few terms such as kur "horse."' plus a listing line 'Seb-Seliyer, endonym; isolate Gypsy dialect, local dialect base'. Live iranicaonline.org could not be reached by automated download; read from the Internet Archive copy of 2023…
